teams.heading: Fiji's Koli Sewabu says FRU is tracking Mark Nawaqanitawase's possible switch
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase has yet to confirm his international allegiance, and Fiji's union is now watching closely. FRU chief executive Koli Sewabu said: "We are aware of the potential switch Mark could make at the next World Cup and follow this with interest." The winger's agent has said he is weighing a possible switch, and he is eligible for Fiji, Italy and Australia after his three-year stand-down. Wallabies coach Les Kiss says he will wait until the end of the year to see where the player sits.

lead.why: The Nawaqanitawase storyline is still open, and Fiji's union has now publicly said it is following the situation.

teams.heading: England women's 41-match unbeaten run ends, Mitchell's side beaten 24-21 by Canada
teams.body: The Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ended in Toronto, where Canada came back to win 24-21 thanks to Shoshanah Seumanutafa's try three minutes from time. It was England's first defeat since November 2022, when New Zealand beat them in the World Cup final, and Canada's first win over them since 2016. Coach John Mitchell said: "We're disappointed by the result but there was some very good things in our performance. So we'll stick to our processes."

lead.why: A new result on the England women's side ending a 41-match unbeaten run is the story fans are discussing, and no men's item of comparable weight is in the pack.

teams.heading: France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey temporarily denied UK entry at Bristol Airport
teams.body: Four Bordeaux Bègles players, including France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey, were stranded at Bristol Airport ahead of their Investec Champions Cup opener against Gloucester. Loosehead prop Matis Perchaud, loose forward Romain Gardrat and Tonga tighthead prop Toma Taufa were held with him, along with a fitness coach, over an administrative problem: their electronic travel permits were linked to passports renewed earlier this year, with no new authorisations obtained. The club contacted the French embassy in London, the issue was eventually resolved, and the players rejoined their teammates.

lead.why: The Lions story is already reported, and the rankings piece casts France as a bystander, so this is the strongest France-centred item left in the pack.

teams.heading: Jack Conan hurts wrist at Clermont, a blow before Ireland's Nations return
teams.body: Leinster's 48-23 win over Clermont in Pool 1 of the Investec Champions Cup came with a cost for Ireland: number eight Jack Conan left with a wrist injury. Planet Rugby called it the only sour note, with Ireland's Nations Championship campaign resuming three weeks on. Sam Prendergast, scoring 14 points, is back in the conversation at fly-half, with Jack Crowley currently sidelined.

lead.why: A new injury to Ireland's Jack Conan is a national-side story, and it is not the Connacht item already run today.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 at home to South Africa in November 2025
teams.body: Italy's last meeting with South Africa ended in a 32-14 home defeat in November 2025, an International Friendlies fixture. It is a single result, not a head-to-head record. Italy's most recent game was a 10-57 defeat to Australia in Round three, and South Africa are next in Round four. In the log, Italy are three defeats from three, with 37 points scored and 131 conceded.

teams.heading: Caity Mattinson, former Scotland women's scrum-half, named Scottish Rugby pathways skills coach
teams.body: Scotland women's pathway just got a fresh voice: Caity Mattinson, who won 37 caps as a scrum-half before retiring in September 2025, has been appointed Scottish Rugby's new Pathways Skills Coach. Her remit covers talent identification, player profiling and specialist kicking and half-back coaching across the women's National Talent Pathway and National Academy. She also worked with Scotland Women's U21s during the 2026 Six Nations. "I can’t wait to get started."

teams.heading: Argentina lead four-nation South American bid for 2035 Rugby World Cup
teams.body: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Brazil have submitted a joint bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, reported in early October, with Los Pumas leading the four-nation push. A Spanish bid, reported as the front-runner with a final at the Nou Camp, is also in contention, and South Africa are listed as a dark horse. Planet Rugby's headline frames the South American bid as a challenge to World Rugby's desire for a European return.

teams.heading: Les Kiss calls Wallabies' first-half display unacceptable after All Blacks loss
teams.body: Les Kiss has called the Wallabies' first half in Saturday's second Bledisloe Test unacceptable, after the All Blacks ran in seven tries to win 43-21 at Accor Stadium. "It's just not acceptable what was put out there," the coach said, pointing to errors his side must stop making. Saturday's result was Australia's 13th straight loss to New Zealand and came a week after a 50-19 defeat at Eden Park. Captain Harry Wilson said the team must start better and cannot keep having terrible halves against the All Blacks.

lead.why: A new coach reaction from Les Kiss on the Wallabies' Sydney defeat, a different angle from the already-run Sua'ali'i and rankings stories.

teams.heading: Japan beat USA 63-14 in September, their biggest win in last 11
teams.body: Across their last 11 matches, Japan have scored 309 points and conceded 308, averaging 28.1 for and 28 against per game. Their most recent match was a 15-42 defeat to France in Round 3. Their biggest win in that window came as a 63-14 home victory over USA in September, in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage.

teams.heading: All Blacks beat Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney for 13th straight win
teams.body: Saturday's Bledisloe test in Sydney delivered New Zealand's 13th straight win over the Wallabies, 43-21 at Accor Stadium. The All Blacks scored seven tries to Australia's three, with Beauden Barrett and Josh Moorby each grabbing a brace, while Rieko Ioane, Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi also crossed. It followed a 50-19 win at Eden Park that kept the Bledisloe Cup for the 24th consecutive year.

lead.why: A fresh result story on the national side's Bledisloe win, which the pack's TMO and Vaa'i pieces have not already covered.

teams.heading: Springbok Cameron Hanekom crosses as Bulls rout Stade Français 56-20 in Champions Cup
teams.body: Cameron Hanekom scored a try as the Bulls beat Stade Français 56-20 in their Champions Cup opener on Saturday, with Cheswill Jooste completing a hat-trick. Hanekom's try came three minutes before the break and he is in a rich vein of form for his club. Planet Rugby says he still has to wait for the number eight shirt, with Jasper Wiese, 30, a favourite of the Bulls' gun team.
